title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 25
statement: How many distinct four-digit numbers are divisible by \(3\) and have \(23\) as their last two digits?

solutions.text:
Write the number as \(\overline{ab23}.\) It is divisible by \(3\) when \(a+b+2+3=a+b+5\) is divisible by \(3,\) that is, when \(a+b\equiv 1 \pmod 3.\)

The two-digit prefix \(\overline{ab}\) ranges over the \(90\) values from \(10\) to \(99,\) and exactly one third of them satisfy this, giving \(\dfrac{90}{3}=30.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: A number is divisible by \(3\) exactly when its digit sum is divisible by \(3\)
Writing the number as \(\overline{ab23},\) require \(a+b+5\) divisible by \(3,\) so \(a+b\equiv 1 \pmod 3\)
